chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Hashim, from Abi Khadija, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The supplication before the emergence of the sun and before its setting is a Sunnah, an Obligation with the emergence of the dawn and the Maghrib.

You should be saying, ‘There is no god except Allah, Alone, there being no associates for Him. The Kingdom is for Him, and for Him is the Praise. He Causes to live and He Causes to die, and He Causes to die and He Causes to live, and He is Living and will not be dying. In His Hand is the goodness, and He is Able over everything’, ten times.

And you should be saying, ‘I seek Refuge with Allah, the Hearing, the Knowing, from the suggestion of the Satan; and I seek Refuge with You, Lord, that they would be approaching me. Allah, He is the Hearing, the Knowing’, ten times before the emergence of the sun and before the setting.
So if you were to forget, so make up for it just as you make up for the Salat when you forget it.

key_terms.بِيَدِهِ الْخَيْرُ: In His Hand is the goodness
key_terms.لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: There is no god except Allah
key_terms.يُحْيِي وَ يُمِيتُ: He Causes to live and He Causes to die

ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed supplication and method for morning and evening remembrance in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this hadith from al-Kafi establishes the 'Morning and Evening Adhkar' as a highly emphasized practice, with the narrator describing it as a 'necessary sunnah' (sunnah wajibah) to maintain spiritual protection throughout the day. The specific dhikr combines attributes of divine sovereignty and refuge from Shaytan, reflecting the daily rhythm of creation and the constant need for divine guardianship against minor distractions. The provision for making it up if forgotten underscores its importance as a consistent spiritual discipline rather than a rigidly time-bound ritual.

en.hubeali:
From him, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Abdul Rahman Bin Abu Hashim, from Abu Khadeeja, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
The supplication before the emergence of the sun and before its setting is a Sunnah, an Obligation with the emergence of the dawn and the Maghrib.

You should be saying, ‘There is no god except Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, Alone, there being no associates for Him<sup>azwj</sup>. The Kingdom is for Him<sup>azwj</sup>, and for Him<sup>azwj</sup> is the Praise. He<sup>azwj</sup> Causes to live and He<sup>azwj</sup> Causes to die, and He<sup>azwj</sup> Causes to die and He<sup>azwj</sup> Causes to live, and He<sup>azwj</sup> is Living and will not be dying. In His<sup>azwj</sup> Hand is the goodness, and He<sup>azwj</sup> is Able over everything’, ten times.

And you should be saying, ‘I seek Refuge with Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, the Hearing, the Knowing, from the suggestion of the Satan<sup style="font-weight: normal">la</sup>; and I seek Refuge with You<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, Lord<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, that they would be approaching me. Allah<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup>, He<sup style="font-weight: normal">azwj</sup> is the Hearing, the Knowing’, ten times before the emergence of the sun and before the setting.
So if you were to forget, so make up for it just as you make up for the Salat when you forget it’.
en.sarwar: 31. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Muhammad ibn Ali from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn abu Hashim from abu Khadijah from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:
“Prayer before sunrise and sunset is an established Sunnah (tradition).

At sunrise and sunset say, ‘No one deserves to be worshipped except Allah, alone, Who has no partner. To Him belongs the Kingdom and all praise. He gives life, causes death, causes death and gives life and He does not die. In His hand is all good, He has power over all things,’ ten times

and then say, ‘I seek protection with Allah, the Hearing, the Omniscient, against the whispers of Satan. I seek protection with You, my Lord against their approaching me. Allah is All-Hearing and Omniscient,’ ten times before sunrise and sunset.
If you forget, make it up as you make up the formal prayer when you forget.’”
